html:
SMTO-CTR-0016 — The task plan is too large for SMTO to accept

GUID: 08d03f30-5e93-49f3-9458-68bf3abcc6b6
Slug: task-contract-size-limit
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • The plan SMTO wrote for your request (its Task Contract) came out larger than SMTO allows, usually because one request asks for a lot at once. SMTO didn't act on this plan.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Break your request into a few smaller requests, each with one clear goal, for example one per folder, server or report. Each smaller request produces a shorter plan that fits within SMTO's size limit.
  2. Remove long pasted text, lists or logs from the request. Attach them as files with Add context instead, if the task needs them. Long pasted text gets copied into the plan and makes it much bigger.
  3. Send the first smaller request as a new message, and wait for it to finish before sending the next. After the request is smaller it's safe to try again, and running the parts in order keeps them easy to check.

What success looks like

  • The new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same large request unchanged; it will be too large every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract's canonical encoded size exceeds MAX_CONTRACT_BYTES (48,000 bytes) in TaskContract model validation or offline validate_contract.

What this means

  • Contract model validation or explicit offline validation measures canonical encoded contract bytes above MAX_CONTRACT_BYTES. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Contract model validation or explicit offline validation measures canonical encoded contract bytes above MAX_CONTRACT_BYTES.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure canonical contract bytes and identify excessive content without dropping required intent silently.

How to fix it

  • Measure len(canonical(contract).encode()) against MAX_CONTRACT_BYTES (48,000) in src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract_models.py; the size_limit reason comes from TaskContract.validate_structure or validate_contract. Reduce the source scope or split the work into separate tasks so each contract fits, without silently dropping required intent; do not raise the limit as a routine fix.
  • Deliberately reduce or split contract content while preserving source requirements and bounded references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A complete appropriately scoped contract fits its supported encoded size.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
